solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pair of coppers with award, right? It's long and thin

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, taken twice for a pair
the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A pair of police officers receive an honour, and someone asks a question about something long and thin.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests policemen, but 'coppers' are the chemical element; the question mark and exclamation turn into a playful definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: A cucumber is a salad vegetable known for its elongated, slender shape, so the description fits.

clue.text: Social convention in practice

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an accepted tradition of a society
second meaning: a habitual way of doing things

explanation.walkthrough: 'In practice' reads as a set phrase, but 'in' just links the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is both a traditional social habit and a person's usual way of behaving.

clue.text: Move fast in pursuit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to rush headlong, as a verb
second meaning: an occupation one follows through life

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a chase; 'pursuit' here means a profession.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to hurtle along uncontrolled, and a career is one's chosen line of work.

clue.text: Boss losing heart? There's food here!

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the word drops out

parts.note: a manager is the boss at work

explanation.surface: A dispirited boss is cheered by finding something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A manger is a trough from which horses and cattle eat their feed.

clue.text: They choose electronic reader at event's beginning

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
a lector reads lessons aloud in church or lectures at a university
taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: first letter of event

explanation.surface: Voters choose an e-reader at the start of some sale.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the body of voters who choose representatives at an election.

clue.text: Busy, new tech in charge

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so the letters that follow come in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
IC is the usual abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A newly installed computer system in charge makes for a busy office.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectic schedule is one crammed with activity, so hectic is a synonym of busy.

clue.text: Profitable firm in income shake-up

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside its letters
a shake-up reorganises things, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written before shuffling
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A company makes money after reorganising its revenue streams.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic venture is one that pays its way, giving a return on outlay.

clue.text: Pattern of work for short period, after hours

parts.note: to temp is to do temporary work
late means after the usual time

explanation.surface: A schedule of short-term shifts worked in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a model or guide shape from which copies are made.

clue.text: Referring to kitchen in urinal unfortunately — extremely coy about that!

indicators.note: going about something surrounds it, so these outer letters wrap the rest
extremely points to the extreme ends of the next word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of coy

indicators.note: things that go unfortunately go wrong, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written before shuffling

explanation.surface: Someone is bashful about a cooking item ending up in a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Culinary is the adjective for cooking and the kitchen.

clue.text: One moving fast has second item of office equipment

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a machine that puts documents on paper

explanation.surface: Somebody dashing about the office has a second printer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter is a runner who races over short distances at top speed.

clue.text: Some wigeon or mallard is common

indicators.note: only some of the words that follow are used, so the answer sits as a portion within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of wigeon, all of or, and the start of mallard

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's remark that some of these ducks are a common sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Wigeon and mallard are both ducks, which makes the clue read like a field guide.
explanation.definitionFit: Something normal is ordinary or usual, which is what common means here.

clue.text: Out of order to repeat light show?

indicators.note: something out of order is not in its proper sequence, so the letters must be rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: It is against the rules to rerun a lighting display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light show' suggests lasers and lamps, but it means a light-hearted stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short comic opera, a theatrical entertainment in a light musical style.

clue.text: Regularly people lie in — it causes problems for some

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and every second letter after

explanation.surface: People who often sleep late cause trouble for others.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollen triggers hay fever, so it brings misery to allergy sufferers but not to everyone.

clue.text: Beginner cool after program torn

parts.note: an app is a software program
rent is an old past participle of rend, to tear
to ice is to chill

explanation.surface: A novice coder chills out after a program gets ripped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places cool at the end, behind the program and torn pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice is a learner of a trade, someone just starting out.

clue.text: Favouring minister (no saint!) or business owner?

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: 'no' tells us to take the saint's abbreviation away from the minister

parts.note: a priest is a minister of religion
S is the abbreviation for saint
taken as written

explanation.surface: Should we back the clergyman, who is no saint, or the businessman?
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor is the owner of a shop, hotel or other business.

clue.text: Not lacking good grades in German and model of industry

parts.note: A and B are the top two exam grades
und is the German word for and
the ant is proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: A student with high marks in German and a hard-working role model.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abundant is plentiful, the opposite of being in short supply.

clue.text: Biscuit's colour captivating Bill

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: maroon is a brownish-crimson colour
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill is charmed by the colour of a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a sweet almond or coconut biscuit.

clue.text: Guardian maybe at first is criticising atomic plant

parts.note: a guardian angel; maybe flags the example

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the words that follow

parts.note: first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A newspaper criticises a nuclear power station.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is a British newspaper, so the surface is about press criticism of an atomic plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelica is an aromatic plant whose candied stems decorate cakes.

clue.text: Intense discussion as British weather not pleasant?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a downpour with wind is unpleasant weather

explanation.surface: A heated debate about the miserable British weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainstorm is a session where a group throws out ideas intensively to solve a problem.

clue.text: Oppose sister for a change

indicators.note: a change means the order is altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before shuffling

explanation.surface: A sibling disagrees just to be different.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to fight against or withstand, which is to oppose.

clue.text: Male animal abandoning cold and old fruit

indicators.note: the animal abandons the letter, which is dropped from it

parts.note: a tomcat is a male cat
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A tomcat leaves behind some cold, stale fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomato is botanically a fruit, a berry of the nightshade family.

clue.text: One having obligation coming up formally dressed, taking time inside

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read upwards, from bottom to top
taking something in means accepting it within, so one word holds the other
inside completes the instruction: the letter is held within the other word

parts.note: wearing official robes
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone due at a formal occasion gets dressed up, taking their time.
explanation.definitionFit: A debtor owes money, so they have a financial obligation.

clue.text: Tidy? Initially not taken in

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: first letter of not
food taken in has been eaten

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether things are tidy and is told no, at first not swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' could mean deceived, but here it means consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: To neaten is to make tidy, so the verb tidy fits.

clue.text: Covering letter? It might be

parts.note: surface reading: a note sent with a job application or CV
setter's reading: the paper wrapper that literally covers a posted letter

explanation.walkthrough: A covering letter is a familiar office phrase, but read literally the clue asks for the thing that covers a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An envelope is the paper sleeve in which correspondence is sealed for posting.

clue.text: Good-looker in a party — it might be tempting to go back

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a party or social event

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so this word is read from its end

parts.note: a sin is what temptation leads to

explanation.surface: A handsome man at a party might tempt someone to return.
explanation.walkthrough: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: An Adonis is a very handsome young man, named after the youth of Greek myth.

clue.text: Wary at living strangely

indicators.note: done strangely means done oddly, so the letters come out in an unusual order

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Someone cautious about living in an odd way.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigilant means watchful and alert for danger, close in sense to wary.

clue.text: Horse not backed in National

indicators.note: backed suggests moving backwards, so the words are read from right to left

parts.note: a nag is an old or poor horse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A horse that nobody bet on running in the Grand National.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's famous steeplechase horse race, which makes 'National' look like the race; here it means a citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tongan is a citizen of the Pacific kingdom of Tonga, a national of that country.

clue.text: Following tour as alternative to being found nearby

parts.note: next means coming after
to do a place is to tour it as a sightseer
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Instructions about which tour to follow if something can be found nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Next door describes the adjacent house, so something next door is very close at hand.
